newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan Jan industry production index at record-MITI.
newsitem.headline: Japan Jan industry production index at record-MITI.

text.p: Japan's industrial production index for January rose to a record high of 105.5, an official of the Ministry of International Trade and Industry (MITI) told reporters on Thursday.
The shipment index for January also rose to a record high of 108.1.
The previous record high for the output index was 103.5 in May 1991, and for the shipment index the previous record was 103.0 in both October 1990 and October 1996.
The official said production rose in all industries in January for the first time since November 1994.
Higher production of telecommunications equipment, air conditioners, cars and printers made the biggest contribution to the increase, he said.

The official attributed the rise in industrial production data to an increase in demand ahead of a rise in consumption tax in April, good exports and an increase in capital spending by information-related industries.
The consumption tax is to be raised to five percent from three percent.

He attributed the lower forecast for manufacturers' output in February to higher-than-expected growth in output in January. The February forecast was for a fall of 3.3 percent month-on-month from a previous forecast of 2.9 percent.
Production of automobiles and transport equipment is expected to fall in February by 13.9 percent from the previous month, against an earlier forecast of a fall of 5.6 percent, he said.
The downward revision was mainly due to a fire at a company supplying parts to Toyota Motor Corp.
If industrial production in the January-March quarter grows by 1.6 percent quarter-on-quarter as predicted by MITI, it would be the third consecutive quarter of growth in output.
